title: A bridge to the other person
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Do you lead the conversation or follow it?

groups.heading: From who I am to who they are

lines.text: I said that the chapter creates a bridge between who we are and who the other person is, now that we understand a little about how we are.
I used a picture of a butterfly going from flower to flower, and you go with a net to bring it back to where you want it, which is a picture of guiding a conversation.
A student said that before a meeting he runs through two or three points or anchors he has practiced, and knows that if he gets them across it will be a success.
I said that step one is really hard when you have a fixed goal, like a retainer or a sale, and described someone who kept repeating the same thing about selling and was not listening.
Another said that such a person is just thinking about themselves, and judgment is clouded.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the two or three points you would get across.
Write the goal you want from the meeting.
Write how you will guide without pushing.
Write what the other person is trying to say.
Write how you will tell they feel heard.

check.q: What did I say the chapter creates?
choices: A bridge between who we are and who they are

check.q: What did I say about a fixed goal?

recap: Build a bridge. Know your points. Listen first.
